live_release_divergence.question: does animedia.icu run the release the adapter was built from?
live_release_divergence.reading: another contour repointed animedia-01 at efdef56 and did not restart the service, so the process still executes fac5643. The site therefore has a restart pending that is not ours and that changes page output on its own.
live_release_divergence.consequence_for_this_pilot: the first prepared adapter was built from fac5643. Applying it would have moved the site off efdef56 — a rollback of somebody else's UX work arriving as a side effect of switching comments on.
live_release_divergence.action: adapter rebuilt from efdef56; a precondition now refuses an adapter whose base disagrees with the live symlink
live_release_divergence.measured_with: curl --resolve animedia.icu:443:127.0.0.1 against real nginx; readlink of the site symlink; template manifest read directly

delta_against_base.note: additive only — the player, the community section and the recommendation shelf of the UX rebuild keep their order and markup; the mount point is appended after them

verification_on_the_rebuilt_release.contour: shadow — real Animedia runtime with the rebuilt adapter, real comments gateway, router mimicking the nginx location split

disk_exhaustion.found: the filesystem holding /, /srv, /home and /tmp reached 100% of 203.3G during this cycle
disk_exhaustion.how_it_presented: not as ENOSPC but as a Chromium renderer crash mid-navigation, reported by the acceptance suite as a failed route check — which reads as a defect in the release
disk_exhaustion.time_to_true_cause: one additional run; the ENOSPC line appeared only after the trace writer also failed
disk_exhaustion.largest_consumer: /tmp/pytest-of-claude/pytest-3133 — 10.75G of pytest temp directories, 7 hours without a write
disk_exhaustion.freed_by_this_session: 10.90G, by removing pytest temp directories older than 3 hours
disk_exhaustion.permanent_fix: apply now gates on free space before any mutation (BLOCKED_DISK_SPACE under 2048MB on /srv), with three tests pinning that the gate exists, precedes every mutation, and compares against a real threshold
disk_exhaustion.note: the suite failure was environmental. The release was not at fault, and the test was not adjusted to pass — it passes unchanged once there is room.

harness_defects_fixed.what: the shadow rehearsal carried a literal release path
harness_defects_fixed.effect: it kept exercising the adapter built from fac5643 after apply had been rebuilt onto efdef56 — a rehearsal of a different artifact than the one being shipped
harness_defects_fixed.fix: the release id is declared once, in the script that deploys it; the rehearsal reads it from there
harness_defects_fixed.pinned_by: TestRehearsalTestsTheShippedRelease — forbids a hardcoded release path and asserts both resolve to the same id

harness_defects_fixed.what: the shadow router printed a full traceback for every BrokenPipeError
harness_defects_fixed.effect: ordinary Chromium navigation cancellation produced ~40 tracebacks that buried the one real failure well below the fold
harness_defects_fixed.fix: connection-reset and broken-pipe are handled as the ordinary traffic they are; every other exception still surfaces

root_access.reason: sudo is outside this session's UNATTENDED_SAFE permission profile, not refused by sudoers
root_access.consequence: the stray nginx backup and the apply run remain one owner command; everything provable without root was proved

stray_nginx_backup.why_it_matters: /etc/nginx/lords/*.conf is an include glob, so the backup loads as a second server block
stray_nginx_backup.resolution: apply quarantines it into /srv/site-factory/var/comments/backups/ as its first privileged act and never deletes it; nginx_backup_path() makes writing a backup into an include directory unreachable rather than merely discouraged

second_domain.guard: apply refuses if animedia-02 resolves to the release directory; rollback acts on no second-domain path
